properties.name: A read tool whose reply outgrows what a client accepts offers a way to bound it, and never goes quiet to fit
properties.statement:
Any tool whose reply can exceed what a client will accept offers a bound (`budget_chars`), and a bounded reply withholds PROSE while never changing a count, a total or an id. A shorter answer is never a quieter one.

TWO KINDS OF PAYLOAD, and the distinction is the requirement rather than a detail:
 · A REPORT may be trimmed — its prose is commentary on counts and ids the reader acts on.
 · A DOCUMENT may NOT. Half an export, half an instruction set or half a published surface reads exactly like a whole one, and nothing in the reply would say otherwise. Such a tool must WITHHOLD WHOLE over budget and name the narrower call that works, never truncate.

COMPLETENESS IS PART OF THE ANSWER WHERE IT IS THE ANSWER. A vocabulary, or a catalogue something picks from, must come back complete even when its prose is dropped entirely. Shortening such a list is forbidden rather than merely discouraged: a list of 1 that is shaped like a list of 65 is the worst possible reply.

WHY THIS IS INTENT AND NOT A FIX: the failure is not a slow call, it is the CLIENT refusing the payload — at which point the session sees harness text and reflow2 never gets to suggest narrowing. A reader who receives nothing cannot be told to narrow their question.

AND IT MUST BE CHECKED AS A CLASS. Three tools carried a bound for months while 178 did not, each fixed by hand after somebody personally met it. A golden-file check cannot catch this, because it pins the tools that exist; a NEW tool returning 126 KB unbounded is a clean diff and a green build.
